name: Diaphragmatic breathing
line: Slow breaths low into the belly. The place to start.
how: Sit or lie down with one hand on your belly.
Breathe in through the nose and let the belly rise.
Breathe out slowly and let the belly fall. The chest stays quiet.
benefits: Helps you use more of your lungs
best: Any time you feel wound up, or when you're new to breathwork.

name: Three-part breath
line: Fill the belly, ribs and chest, then let it all go.
how: Breathe in through the nose, filling the belly first.
Keep filling so the ribs widen, then the upper chest.
Breathe out slowly from the top down.
benefits: Builds awareness of the whole breath
best: Before a long meditation, or when your breathing feels shallow.

name: Ujjayi
line: A soft ocean sound at the back of the throat.
how: Breathe through the nose with the lips closed.
Slightly narrow the back of the throat, as if fogging a mirror with your mouth shut.
Keep the soft sound going on the way in and the way out.
best: Steadying yourself before focused work, or alongside yoga.
care: Keep the throat soft. If it feels strained, make the sound quieter.

name: Nadi Shodhana
line: Alternate nostrils with a gentle pause. A classic for balance.
how: Rest your right thumb by the right nostril and your ring finger by the left.
Close the right and breathe in through the left. Close both and hold briefly.
Release the right and breathe out. Breathe in through the right, hold, and breathe out through the left. That's one round.
benefits: Traditionally said to balance the two sides of the brain and clear energy channels
best: Feeling scattered or pulled in two directions.
care: Skip the hold if it feels uncomfortable, or if you're pregnant or have high blood pressure. Best with a clear nose.

name: Anulom Vilom
line: Smooth alternate nostril breathing with no holds.
how: Use your right thumb and ring finger to close one nostril at a time.
In through the left, out through the right.
In through the right, out through the left. Keep it smooth and quiet.
benefits: Traditionally said to purify energy channels
best: A gentler way into alternate nostril breathing.

name: Kapalabhati
line: Short, sharp exhales from the belly. Wakes you right up.
how: Sit tall. Breathe out sharply through the nose by snapping the belly in.
Let the in-breath happen by itself. Follow the ticks.
After each round, take a full breath, hold it comfortably, let it go, and breathe freely.
benefits: Traditionally used to clear the airways
best: A sluggish morning. Best on an empty stomach.
care: Avoid if you're pregnant or have high blood pressure, heart disease, epilepsy, a hernia, recent surgery or a panic disorder. Sit down, and stop if you feel dizzy.

name: Bhastrika
line: Deep, forceful breaths in and out, like a bellows.
how: Sit tall with a straight spine.
Breathe in and out through the nose, deeply and vigorously, with the same force each way. Follow the ticks.
After each round, take a full breath, hold it comfortably, let it go, and rest.
best: When you need a real lift and you're already comfortable with Kapalabhati.
care: Avoid if you're pregnant or have high blood pressure, heart disease, epilepsy, glaucoma, a hernia or a panic disorder. Always sit down, never do it near water or while driving, and stop if you feel dizzy or tingly.

name: Breath of fire
line: Fast, even nose breaths powered from the belly.
how: Sit tall with your mouth closed.
Breathe quickly through the nose, in and out at equal strength, pumping from the navel. Follow the ticks or go slower.
Rest and breathe normally between rounds.
best: A short burst of energy, for people used to fast breathing.
care: Avoid if you're pregnant or have high blood pressure, heart disease, epilepsy or a panic disorder. Always sit down, never do it near water or while driving, and stop if you feel dizzy or tingly.

name: Bhramari
line: A soft hum on every exhale, like a bee.
how: Sit comfortably and close your eyes. You can gently cover your ears.
Breathe in through the nose.
Breathe out with a steady, low hum, lips together and teeth apart.
best: A racing mind, or the last few minutes before bed.
care: Skip it with an ear infection. Don't press on your ears.

name: Sitali
line: Breathe in over a curled tongue to cool down.
how: Curl the sides of your tongue into a tube and let the tip stick out a little.
Breathe in through the tongue and feel the coolness.
Close your mouth and breathe out through the nose.
best: Hot days, after exercise, or when you're irritated. Not everyone can curl their tongue, so try Sitkari if you can't.
care: Skip it in cold air or with a cold, asthma or low blood pressure.

name: Sitkari
line: Breathe in through the teeth for the same cooling feel.
how: Bring your teeth gently together and part your lips.
Breathe in through the teeth with a soft hiss.
Close your mouth and breathe out through the nose.
best: Cooling down if you can't curl your tongue for Sitali.
care: Skip it in cold air, or if you have sensitive teeth or low blood pressure.

name: Surya Bhedana
line: In through the right nostril, out through the left.
how: Close the left nostril with your ring finger and breathe in through the right.
Close the right with your thumb and breathe out through the left.
Repeat, always in on the right.
benefits: Traditionally said to stimulate the metabolism
best: Mornings and cold days. Not close to bedtime.
care: Skip it if you have high blood pressure or heart disease, or if you already feel anxious.

name: Chandra Bhedana
line: In through the left nostril, out through the right.
how: Close the right nostril with your thumb and breathe in through the left.
Close the left with your ring finger and breathe out through the right.
Repeat, always in on the left.
best: Evenings and wind-down time.
care: Skip it if you have low blood pressure or feel low on energy.

name: Square breathing
line: In, hold, out, hold, all for four counts.
how: Breathe in through the nose for four.
Hold for four.
Breathe out for four, then hold empty for four.
best: Before something demanding: a meeting, a hard talk, a decision.
care: If the holds feel uncomfortable, shorten them or leave them out.

name: Triangle breathing
line: In, hold, out. Square breathing without the empty hold.
how: Breathe in through the nose for four.
Hold for four.
Breathe out for four and go straight into the next breath.
benefits: Easier than holding your breath empty
best: When square breathing feels like too much.

name: Visama Vritti
line: Breathe out for twice as long as you breathe in.
how: Breathe in through the nose for four.
Breathe out slowly for eight.
If eight is too long, try three in and six out.
best: Anxiety, or coming down after a stressful day.

name: Coherent breathing
line: About five and a half breaths a minute, smooth and even.
how: Breathe in gently through the nose for five and a half seconds.
Breathe out for the same length, with no pause between.
Keep it light. There's no need for big breaths.
best: A daily habit. It works well for longer sits.

name: 4-7-8 breathing
line: In for four, hold for seven, out for eight.
how: Breathe in quietly through the nose for four.
Hold for seven.
Breathe out through the mouth with a soft whoosh for eight.
benefits: Helps you wind down for sleep
best: In bed, or any time you need to settle quickly.
care: You may feel lightheaded at first. Keep it short and do it sitting or lying down.

name: Physiological sigh
line: Two breaths in, one long breath out. A fast reset.
how: Breathe in through the nose until you're nearly full.
Take one more short sip of air through the nose.
Let it all out slowly through the mouth.
best: A few minutes between things, or right after a stressful moment.

name: Pursed-lip breathing
line: Breathe out through pursed lips, as if cooling soup.
how: Breathe in through the nose for two.
Purse your lips as if you're about to whistle.
Breathe out gently through them for four.
benefits: Helps you feel less out of breath
best: After climbing stairs or exercise, or whenever you feel short of breath.

name: Viloma
line: Breathe in as three sips with small pauses.
how: Breathe in a third of the way and pause.
Breathe in another third and pause, then fill up and pause.
Breathe out slowly and smoothly.
best: When you've got the basics and want something more absorbing.
care: The pauses should feel easy. If you feel short of air, go back to smooth breathing.

name: Breath counting
line: Count each exhale up to ten, then start again.
how: Breathe naturally. Don't try to change anything.
Silently count each out-breath, from one up to ten.
When you lose count, and you will, just go back to one.
best: A wandering mind, or a day when you don't want to work at anything.

name: Natural breath awareness
line: Change nothing. Simply watch the breath.
how: Sit or lie down and let the breath do what it does.
Rest your attention where you feel it most: the nostrils, the chest or the belly.
When your mind wanders, come back to the next breath.
benefits: The foundation of many meditation practices
best: Days when anything more feels like too much.

name: Lion's breath
line: A big open-mouthed exhale. Silly, and it works.
how: Breathe in deeply through the nose.
Open your mouth wide, stick out your tongue and breathe out with a strong "haaa".
Rest for a couple of normal breaths, then repeat.
benefits: Releases tension in the face and jaw
Gives a quick burst of energy
best: When you feel stuck or tense, and nobody's watching.

name: Breath of joy
line: Three quick inhales with your arms, then swing down with a ha.
how: Stand with your feet apart and knees soft.
Breathe in three short sips: arms forward, then out wide, then overhead.
Bend your knees, swing your arms down and let it out with a "ha".
best: A flat afternoon, instead of more coffee.
care: Do this standing, away from anything hard. Skip it if you have high blood pressure, or a head or eye injury. Stop if you feel dizzy.

name: Udgeeth
line: A long, slow Om on every exhale.
how: Sit tall and breathe in deeply through the nose.
Chant a long "Ooo" that closes into "mmm", using the whole breath.
Let the vibration fade before the next breath.
best: Before meditating or going to sleep.

name: Murccha
line: Long holds for deepening meditation. Advanced only.
how: Learn this from a teacher in person first.
Breathe in deeply and hold. This app keeps the hold short and never asks you to go further.
Breathe out softly, hold empty for a moment, and rest between rounds. The traditional practice goes to the edge of fainting, and this version deliberately doesn't.
best: Experienced practitioners, seated, with someone nearby.
care: For experienced practitioners only. Avoid if you're pregnant or have heart disease, high or low blood pressure, epilepsy or dizzy spells. Always sit down, and never do it near water or while driving. Stop right away if you feel lightheaded.

name: Plavini
line: Fill the belly to the maximum and hold. Advanced only.
how: Learn this from a teacher in person first.
Breathe in slowly, filling the belly as far as it comfortably goes, and hold.
Breathe out slowly and rest between rounds. The traditional practice also involves swallowing air, which this app doesn't guide.
benefits: Traditionally associated with buoyancy and energy control
best: Experienced practitioners, on an empty stomach.
care: For experienced practitioners only. Avoid if you're pregnant or have heart disease, high blood pressure, a hernia, reflux or stomach problems. Sit down, and stop if you feel any discomfort or lightheadedness.
